questions.question: Describe where ancient Egypt was and when it existed.
questions.expected_answer: Ancient Egypt was in north-eastern Africa, along the Nile River, which flows north through the desert into the Mediterranean Sea. About five thousand one hundred years ago, Upper Egypt in the south and Lower Egypt in the north were united into one kingdom under one king, later called a pharaoh. The society lasted about three thousand years.

questions.question: Why is ancient Egypt called an African civilisation, and what are some of its achievements?
questions.expected_answer: It grew up in Africa, along an African river, its people were Africans, and it was linked to other African peoples such as Kush. It was a large, organised society with cities, rulers, writing and religion. Its achievements include pyramids and temples, hieroglyphic writing, mathematics, a calendar, medicine and papyrus paper.

questions.question: Name four kinds of sources that tell us about ancient Egypt.
questions.expected_answer: Buildings such as pyramids, temples and tombs, with wall paintings and carvings; writing on stone, papyrus and pottery; objects such as tools, pots, jewellery and toys found by archaeologists; and mummies. Writings by visitors such as Herodotus also help. The dry desert preserved many of them.
